name: native-alert-dialog
description: A confirmation modal the user must answer. The scrim does not dismiss it. Renders through a PortalHost mounted in the app's root layout.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Default open state for uncontrolled usage

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired on open state change: (open: boolean) => void

props.name: portalHost
props.description: Name of the PortalHost to render into. Only needed when the app mounts more than one.

slots.name: children
slots.description: AlertDialogTrigger + AlertDialogContent (with Header, Footer, Action, Cancel)

examples.title: Destructive confirmation
examples.description: Cancel first, destructive action second — the phone convention
examples.code:
<AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogTitle>Delete account?</AlertDialogTitle>
    <AlertDialogDescription>
      Everything in this account is removed. This cannot be undone.
    </AlertDialogDescription>
    <View className="flex-row justify-end gap-2">
      <AlertDialogCancel asChild>
        <Button variant="secondary"><Text>Cancel</Text></Button>
      </AlertDialogCancel>
      <AlertDialogAction asChild>
        <Button variant="destructive" onPress={remove}><Text>Delete</Text></Button>
      </AlertDialogAction>
    </View>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>

examples.title: Opened from a trigger
examples.description: Let the alert own its state
examples.code:
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="destructive"><Text>Leave team</Text></Button>
  </AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogTitle>Leave this team?</AlertDialogTitle>
    <AlertDialogDescription>You will lose access to its projects.</AlertDialogDescription>
    <View className="flex-row justify-end gap-2">
      <AlertDialogCancel asChild>
        <Button variant="secondary"><Text>Stay</Text></Button>
      </AlertDialogCancel>
      <AlertDialogAction asChild>
        <Button variant="destructive"><Text>Leave</Text></Button>
      </AlertDialogAction>
    </View>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>

ai.whenToUse: Use to confirm something irreversible before it happens: delete, archive, leave, revoke. Always pair a Cancel with the confirming Action, and say the consequence in the description.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for anything the user can undo — show the result with an undo affordance instead of asking first. Don't use it to carry a form (that is Dialog). Don't use it for information with only one button; that is a message, not a question.
commonMistakes: Forgetting <PortalHost /> in the root layout — the alert mounts but renders nothing at all
Expecting a scrim tap to dismiss it: an alert dialog deliberately ignores that, so a missing Cancel leaves the user stuck
Confirming a recoverable action, which trains users to dismiss the dialog without reading it
Writing the title as a statement instead of a question, so the two buttons have no question to answer
Labelling the buttons OK and Cancel rather than naming the action — Delete next to Cancel is unambiguous when read aloud out of context
ai.accessibilityNotes: The panel is announced as an alert when it opens, with the title as its name — always include AlertDialogTitle, and put the consequence in AlertDialogDescription so it is read with the question. Because the scrim does not dismiss, a Cancel control is mandatory rather than a courtesy: it is the only exit for a screen-reader or keyboard user. Name buttons after their effect so each is unambiguous when announced alone.
